research_mode: official ONS, Home Office, Office for Statistics Regulation and Police.uk web sources only; API throttling and area limits, unmapped-record completeness, location anonymisation, quality assurance, boundary resolution, statistical-geography version and administrative-data assurance guards; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police API call limits
verified_claims: the API uses a leaky-bucket rate controller
the current limit is 15 requests per second with a burst of 30
exceeding the rate limit returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests
limitations: rate-limit compliance is an acquisition-control requirement and not evidence quality
retries must be bounded and must not duplicate or silently omit source months

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Street-level crimes API contract
verified_claims: street-level crime can be requested within one mile of a point or within a custom polygon
custom areas containing more than 10000 crimes return HTTP 503
published street-level crime locations are approximate rather than exact
limitations: HTTP 503 requires bounded subdivision or explicit failure evidence
a point or polygon response cannot prove exact parcel incidence

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop and searches by area API contract
verified_claims: stop and searches can be requested within one mile of a point or a custom polygon
GET requests longer than 4094 characters return HTTP 400 and POST is recommended for complex polygons
published stop-and-search locations are approximate
limitations: polygon transport limits must not cause silent truncation
stop and search is police-activity context rather than crime incidence

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crimes with no location API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns crimes that could not be mapped to a location
requests are force, category and optional month scoped
location and location_type are null while the persistent crime identifier and latest outcome may remain available
limitations: unmapped crimes must be counted in completeness diagnostics but cannot be assigned to a parcel or LSOA
the latest month default must be explicitly pinned

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop and searches with no location API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns stop and searches that could not be mapped to a location
requests are force scoped with an optional YYYY-MM month
some forces provide only dates, which can create a disproportionate number of midnight timestamps
limitations: unmapped stop searches cannot be spatially attributed
timestamp concentration at midnight may reflect source precision rather than operational timing

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk data provenance and flow
verified_claims: 43 geographic forces, British Transport Police, Police Service of Northern Ireland and the Ministry of Justice provide data used by the site
forces upload monthly Crime and ASB and Police Outcomes files which undergo quality assurance
court-result matching is performed with Ministry of Justice data before publication and all published data are anonymised
limitations: the data-flow description does not establish that every force-month is complete
court matching and publication QA do not create exact parcel locations

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk location anonymisation methodology
verified_claims: published coordinates represent approximate rather than exact crime locations
exact locations are replaced by the nearest point from a master list whose catchments contain at least eight postal addresses or none
coordinates are zeroed when the nearest map point is more than 20 kilometres away
the snap-point list was refreshed in 2022
limitations: the anonymised point may fall outside the originating force boundary or target statistical area
an anonymised coordinate must never be treated as the incident address or target parcel

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk known data-quality issues
verified_claims: force geocoding accuracy estimates range from 60 to 97 percent
court-result fuzzy-match success rates range from 19 to 97 percent because no unique cross-system crime identifier exists
monthly data are snapshots and later source-system reclassification, false-report confirmation or location change may not reach the site without a full refresh
British Transport Police and Police Service of Northern Ireland do not provide outcome data
limitations: these ranges are system-level limitations and not candidate confidence scores
snapshot mutability and missing outcomes require force-month-specific caveats

sources.name: Digital boundaries
verified_claims: ONS produces full-resolution and generalised digital boundary sets
full and generalised products have different coastal extents including clipped coastline and extent of the realm
BFC, BFE, BGC and BUC products are designed for different analysis or visualisation contexts
products are available under the Open Government Licence with required attribution
limitations: generalised or ultra-generalised boundaries may be unsuitable for exact point-in-polygon joins near edges
boundary type and edition must be pinned and not silently interchanged

sources.name: Statistical geographies
verified_claims: LSOAs are usually groups of four or five Output Areas
2021 LSOAs comprise between 400 and 1200 households and between 1000 and 3000 usual residents
England has 33755 LSOAs and Wales has 1917
boundary sets, names, codes and lookup files are available from the Open Geography portal
limitations: LSOA thresholds describe statistical-area design and not parcel characteristics
England-only joins must reject Welsh codes and record the 2021 geography edition

sources.name: Census 2021 geographies
verified_claims: some 2011 LSOAs changed after Census 2021 because of population and household changes
new 2021 LSOAs were created by merging or splitting 2011 LSOAs
Census 2021 outputs use 2021 LSOAs composed of unchanged and new areas
limitations: 2011 and 2021 LSOA codes and boundaries are not interchangeable
cross-edition comparisons require an explicit lookup or are rejected

sources.name: Administrative Data Quality Assurance Toolkit
verified_claims: the toolkit was last updated on 21 May 2026
it supports assessment of administrative-data quality assurance for official statistics
it requires producers to judge whether administrative data remain suitable and to provide appropriate documentation for users
limitations: the toolkit is a regulatory framework and not direct crime evidence
a QAAD label must not replace source-specific tests or runtime acceptance

sources.name: QAAD assurance expectation for police recorded crime
verified_claims: OSR considers police recorded crime to require comprehensive QAAD assurance because of high quality risk and high public interest
comprehensive assurance expects investigation of supplier arrangements, independent audit evidence and detailed published documentation
both Home Office and force-level quality checks are within scope
limitations: a comprehensive-assurance requirement does not prove that current assurance is complete
force and month evidence must remain separately evaluated

sources.name: Administrative Data Quality Assurance Toolkit QA matrix
verified_claims: the QA matrix separates operational context and data collection, communication with suppliers, supplier QA standards and checks, and the producer's own QA investigations
assurance levels range from no assurance upward and require progressively stronger evidence
limitations: matrix completion must be supported by real documentation and tests
an unverified checklist cannot be promoted as evidence of data accuracy

sources.name: Action plan for improving police recorded crime quality
verified_claims: the Home Office planned in-depth work across a representative group of force IT systems to document strengths, limitations and quality implications
the action plan references a Data Quality Assurance Manual used by force crime registrars for local audits
the Home Office planned annual collection of information on force compliance with minimum QA standards
limitations: planned actions and review dates are not proof of completion
current implementation status requires separate evidence

sources.name: Home Office Annual Data Requirement data privacy information notice
verified_claims: the majority of ADR data received are aggregated
Home Office quality assures data before publication to prevent identification in outputs
police recorded crime data are supplied to and published by ONS in aggregate form quarterly and annually
limitations: aggregated ADR publication cannot establish street or parcel observations
privacy QA and statistical QA are distinct and both limitations must remain explicit
